chunks: And from him from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

In gold, when it reaches twenty dinars, there is half a dinar [in zakat]; and there is nothing in what is less than twenty. And in silver, when it reaches two hundred dirhams, there are five dirhams; and there is nothing in what is less than two hundred. If it increases by thirty-nine over the two hundred, there is nothing in it until it reaches forty; and there is nothing in any of the fractions until it reaches forty. And likewise the dinars are upon this calculation.
As for that which indicates that zakat is only obligatory in it if it is struck [minted], what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the nisab and amount of zakat for gold and silver in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the nisab and zakat amounts for gold and silver, emphasizing that the obligation applies to minted currency (dinar/dirham) rather than raw bullion. It further specifies that fractional coins do not incur zakat until they collectively reach the threshold of forty, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the early Shia school regarding circulating currency.
